## Attempt 1 — MALFORMED SPLICE (rc=126, must not be read as a gate verdict)

pid 2154303. Wrote `rc=126` within ~1 s and NO junit XML. `126` is the shell's
"command found but cannot be invoked" — not a pytest exit code.

Cause: the gate set was sourced from `select_step9c_tests.py --files-only`, which
emits ONE PATH PER LINE. Splicing that into the command TEXT of
`bash -c "... uv run pytest $S9C_FILES ..."` expanded the newlines into the command
string itself, so the inner shell parsed each subsequent path as its own COMMAND.
Log evidence:

```
tests/test_adhoc_summary_disclosure_pins.py .....                        [100%]
============================== 5 passed in 0.26s ===============================
bash: line 2: tests/test_adversarial_planner_factchecker_grain_pin.py: Permission denied
bash: line 3: tests/test_adversarial_planner_warn_disposition.py: Permission denied
... (one per remaining file)
```

Consequences, all benign but each capable of misleading a reader:

- pytest ran **1 of 120 files** (`test_adhoc_summary_disclosure_pins.py`, 5 passed)
  and every other path failed as a bogus command.
- The trailing flags (`--continue-on-collection-errors`, `--junitxml=...`,
  `--basetemp=...`) landed on the LAST bogus line, so the single real pytest
  invocation ran WITHOUT `--junitxml` — which is why no junit XML exists.
- `rc=126` is the exit status of the last bogus command, carrying no information
  about any test.

**The count cross-check passed at 120 and did not catch this.** The canonical
guard computes `S9C_GOT=$(printf '%s\n' $S9C_FILES | grep -c .)`, and unquoted
expansion word-splits on IFS (which includes newline), so a newline-separated list
counts correctly while splicing incorrectly. The guard validates the gate set's
CARDINALITY, not its SPLICE SHAPE. A separate workflow-fix task is being filed for
that hardening; the recipe's own `<files>` placeholder assumes a space-separated
literal, so the deviation was mine.
